clusters.title: ‘What’s the safest way to defrost chicken?’ We’re answering your food safety questions
clusters.neutral_headline: ‘What’s the safest way to defrost chicken?’ We’re answering...

items.title: ‘What’s the safest way to defrost chicken?’ We’re answering your food safety questions
items.standfirst: We’re hosting a live Q&A on 26 October at noon ET (4pm GMT) on the Guardian US site with guest experts Rachel Sherman and Caroline L Schauer. Sign up or sign in to askThe Drexel food lab tested the best air fryers (the Cosori, a hands-down winner), the best nonstick cookware (Our Place, trendy and top of the line) and much moreAdrian from Toronto, Canada asks in a callout question: How do I make my fridge work better? In my mini fridge, cans sometimes get so cold that they explode, and sometimes milk goes bad faster. Is uneven refrigeration something I can improve, or is it just a sign of a bad fridge?Rachel: My first thought here is to make sure your refrigerator is not overfilled. Uneven refrigeration could be due to lack of airflow if you have too much on your shelves. If this is not the case, it would be best to call in a professional. It could be something like a poor seal or an issue with the coils.This is a little out of my expertise so I would definitely get someone in to take a look at it.Rachel: The major concern when defrosting chicken is to stay out of the temperature “danger zone,” or the temperatures at which bacteria can grow most quickly. The USDA identifies as 40F-140F (noting here that before eating, USDA suggests chicken should be cooked to 165F). If you forget to put your chicken in the refrigerator the night before to defrost, you can place your chicken, still sealed, in a bowl of cold water. Make sure you change the water often, or keep it at a slow drip so that the water stays cool.Microwaves can also assist, most have a defrost function, however microwaves do not always cook evenly so if you use this route, it is best to cook it immediately. If you have an instant pot, and are only cooking a few pieces you can find cook from frozen recipes online. Just remember to keep an eye on the danger zone. My advice if you are worried about food safety is to keep a food thermometer in the kitchen (I use the ThermoWorks Thermopop) so you can feel confident about your food safety decisions. Continue reading...

clusters.neutral_headline: The pet I’ll never forget: Clement was hit by a car and left to die in...

items.title: The pet I’ll never forget: Clement was hit by a car and left to die in a ditch – then found his beautiful purpose
items.standfirst: Before being rescued, he had an extremely traumatic experience. You’d never know it though, from the joy his patience and sunny nature bring to those who most need himIn December 2024, my kerry blue terrier, Magnus, died suddenly from a stroke at the age of nine. Devastated, I started looking at rescue dogs on Facebook and came across Clement, who was being looked after by a shelter in Romania. It wasn’t his appearance that caught my attention, but his heartbreaking story.An eight-year-old mixed-breed rescue, Clement had spent most of his life with a woman living with Alzheimer’s. One day, she accidentally let him out. He was hit by a car, attacked by two large dogs and left in a ditch for three days in the snow before being rescued by chance. When I read this, I knew I had to take him in. Continue reading...
